mainTopic: How a person is judged: רבי יצחק's sayings on the שופר, sins, and decrees, and the three books opened on ראש השנה
overview: This amud opens at the end of רבי יצחק's question: why do we blow the שופר while sitting and then again while standing during מוסף? The answer is 'to confuse the שטן.' The גמרא then brings a long series of sayings from רבי יצחק about judgment. A year without שופר at its start ends badly, a year that starts poor ends rich, and a person is judged only by his present deeds. Three things bring up a person's sins. Four things tear up a bad decree: צדקה, crying out, changing one's name, and changing one's deeds. Some add changing one's place. רבי יצחק also teaches two duties of the רגל: to greet one's רבי and to make oneself טהור, which a ברייתא proves with a קל וחומר. The גמרא then returns to ראש השנה with רבי יוחנן's teaching that three books are opened, for the righteous, the wicked, and the בינוניים, and two אמוראים each bring a פסוק for it. Finally, a ברייתא of בית שמאי describes three groups on the final יום הדין, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why do we blow again while standing?
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of רבי יצחק's question: why blow a second set of sounds while standing, after already blowing while sitting?
steps.simpleTranslation: [Why do we blow while sitting,] and then blow תקיעה and תרועה again while standing?
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the last words of a question that started on the previous amud. רבי יצחק asks why we blow the שופר twice, once sitting and once standing. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first set, sitting, already fulfills the מצוה. So the second set, standing during the עמידה, looks extra. רבי יצחק wants to know what that second blowing adds.

keyTerms.meaning: We blow a תקיעה, the long straight sound
We blow a תרועה, the broken sound
While they are standing, meaning during the מוסף עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'כשהן יושבין' (while sitting) came just before. The question is really about why there are TWO sets of blowing.

phrases.english: and [why] do they again sound a tekia and a terua while they are standing?
phrases.notes: Ends the question that began on the previous amud: 'Why do we blow while sitting...'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוֹקְעִין וּמְרִיעִין כְּשֶׁהֵן עוֹמְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a question that began on the previous amud
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for a second set of שופר blasts while standing, when the sitting set already fulfilled the מצוה

steps.title: To confuse the accuser
steps.stepSummary: We blow twice in order to confuse the שטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: In order to confuse the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers his own question. The double blowing is meant to confuse the שטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing more than we have to shows how much כלל ישראל loves the מצוה. Seeing this, the שטן is thrown off, and he cannot argue against us well in the heavenly court. So the second blowing is not about the basic מצוה. It protects us during the judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: The accuser who argues against people in the heavenly court

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for why we blow שופר both before מוסף and during מוסף on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: In order to confuse the Satan.
phrases.notes: The extra love shown for the מצוה silences the accuser.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי לְעַרְבֵּב הַשָּׂטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second blowing is meant to confuse the שטן so he cannot accuse כלל ישראל.

steps.title: No שופר at the start means trouble at the end
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק: a year in which the שופר was not blown at its beginning will suffer bad things at its end.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: any year in which they do not blow the שופר at its beginning, bad will come to it at its end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second saying of רבי יצחק. If the שופר was not blown on ראש השנה, bad things happen at the end of that year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק plays on the word מריעין. It can mean 'blow a תרועה,' and it can also mean 'bring harm' (from the root רע, bad). Missing the תרועה at the start brings 'רעה' at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: At its beginning, meaning ראש השנה
At its end, meaning the end of the year

steps.confusionAlert: Here מריעין does NOT mean 'they blow a תרועה' like in step 1. It means 'bad is brought upon it.' It is a play on words.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzhak said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שָׁנָה שֶׁאֵין תּוֹקְעִין לָהּ בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ —
phrases.english: Any year in which they do not sound the shofar at its beginning,
phrases.notes: For example, when some mishap (אונס) prevented the blowing. This does not refer to ראש השנה on שבת, when not blowing is required by the חכמים and brings no harm.

phrases.english: will suffer evil at its end.
phrases.notes: A play on words: מריעין as 'bring harm.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל שָׁנָה שֶׁאֵין תּוֹקְעִין לָהּ בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2's idea that the שופר confuses the שטן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year without שופר at its start will have misfortune at its end.

steps.title: Why the year ends badly
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that the שטן was not confused, so he was free to accuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the שטן was not confused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind step 3 and answers right away. Without the שופר, the שטן was never confused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties step 3 back to step 2. The שופר is what confuses the שטן. With no שופר, he can bring all his accusations, and that leads to punishment by the end of the year.
steps.whatToRemember: The שופר protects us in judgment because it confuses the שטן. Blowing twice confuses him even more. Not blowing at all leaves him free to accuse.

phrases.english: What is the reason? Because the Satan was not confused.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for step 3's statement
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With no שופר, the שטן was not confused and was able to accuse.

steps.title: A poor start brings a rich ending
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק: a year that starts poor ends rich. He learns this from the missing א in מרשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: any year that is poor at its beginning becomes rich at its end. As it says, 'From the beginning of the year.' The word is written מרשית, without an א, which hints at poverty. 'Until the end' means its end will have a good future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third saying of רבי יצחק, this time with a source in a פסוק. A year that starts poor will end rich.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the word מראשית ('from the beginning') is written without an א, so it can be read as 'from poverty' (רש, a poor person). The second half, 'ועד אחרית,' is read as 'the end will have a good outcome.' So poverty at the start leads to good things at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (the spelling, as opposed to how it is read)
End, or a good future outcome

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מתעשרת (becomes rich) with מעשר (tithes). Here the word comes from עושר, wealth.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzhak said:
Any year that is poor at its beginning
phrases.notes: Poor can also mean humble or troubled, which may lead to humble prayer.

phrases.english: will be made rich at its end,
as it is stated: 'From the beginning of the year' (Deuteronomy 11:12).
phrases.notes: This is how the word is read aloud.

phrases.english: 'Mereishit' is written, without an alef.
phrases.notes: The missing א links the word to רש, poor.

phrases.english: 'And until the end'
means its end will have a good future.
phrases.notes: אחרית is understood as a hopeful outcome.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל שָׁנָה שֶׁרָשָׁה בִּתְחִלָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new saying from the same speaker, on the same theme of how a year turns out
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year that begins poor will end rich, learned from the spelling מרשית and the words ועד אחרית.

steps.title: Judged only by present deeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק: a person is judged only by his deeds at that moment, as we see from ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: a person is judged only by what he is doing at that time. As it says: 'For God heard the voice of the boy where he is.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth saying of רבי יצחק. A person is judged only by how he is acting right now, not by what he will do later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about ישמעאל, dying of thirst in the desert. His descendants would later do evil, but הקב״ה answered him 'באשר הוא שם,' meaning based on where he stood at that moment. This teaches that future sins do not count against a person in today's judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: Where he is, meaning in his present state

steps.whatToRemember: The first four sayings of רבי יצחק are all about judgment. The שופר confuses the שטן. No שופר leads to a bad end. A poor start leads to a rich end. And a person is judged only by his present deeds. The series of רבי יצחק's teachings continues in the next steps.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic idea for ראש השנה: הקב״ה judges us by who we are right now, so תשובה today changes the judgment.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzhak said:
A person is not judged

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה,
phrases.english: except according to his deeds at that time,
phrases.notes: Not according to his future deeds.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי שָׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶל קוֹל הַנַּעַר
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'For God has heard the voice of the lad'
phrases.notes: Genesis 21:17, about ישמעאל.

phrases.english: 'where he is.'
phrases.notes: In his present, innocent state.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אֵין דָּנִין אֶת הָאָדָם אֶלָּא לְפִי מַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another saying from רבי יצחק on the theme of judgment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is judged only by his deeds at the time of judgment, not by future deeds, as shown by ישמעאל.

steps.title: Three things that bring up a person's sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק lists three things that cause Heaven to look into a person's sins: a leaning wall, expecting one's prayer to be answered, and calling for Heaven to judge another person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Three things cause a person's sins to be remembered. They are: a leaning wall, expecting one's prayer to be answered, and handing over judgment against one's fellow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement from רבי יצחק. It lists three behaviors that make Heaven look closely at a person's record.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item puts a person in a spot where Heaven checks whether he deserves to be saved or answered. Standing near a falling wall means relying on a miracle. Expecting an answer to prayer or asking Heaven to punish someone else invites a close look at your own merits.

keyTerms.meaning: cause his sins to be remembered and examined
a leaning wall about to collapse
expecting or counting on one's prayer being answered
calling on Heaven to judge another person

steps.confusionAlert: Here עיון תפלה does NOT mean praying with good concentration, which is praiseworthy. It means sitting back and expecting that Heaven must answer you, as if you deserve it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַזְכִּירִין עֲוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Three things bring up a person's sins,
these are: a leaning wall,
phrases.notes: Standing near danger means relying on a miracle, so Heaven checks whether he deserves one.

phrases.english: and expecting one's prayer to be answered,
and handing over judgment against his fellow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים מַזְכִּירִין עֲוֹנוֹתָיו שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement in the series of רבי יצחק's teachings, following his teaching about being judged by one's current deeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaning walls, expecting prayer to be answered, and calling for judgment on another all cause one's own sins to be examined.

steps.title: Proof from שרה that calling for judgment brings punishment first
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין teaches that whoever calls for Heaven to judge another is punished first. He proves it from שרה, who called for judgment against אברהם and died before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אבין said: Anyone who hands over judgment against his fellow is punished first. As it says: 'And שרי said to אברם: My anger is upon you,' and it is written: 'And אברהם came to eulogize שרה and to weep for her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the third item on רבי יצחק's list with a teaching from רבי אבין and a proof from the פסוקים about שרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרה told אברהם 'let ה׳ judge between me and you.' Later the תורה tells us אברהם mourned for her, which means she died first. רבי אבין reads this as a result of her asking Heaven to judge, because that caused her own deeds to be examined first.

keyTerms.meaning: my anger (or my wrong) is upon you

phrases.english: For Rabbi Avin said:
Anyone who hands over judgment against his fellow,
he is punished first,
as it is said: "And Sarai said to Avram:
My anger is upon you,"
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues: 'let ה׳ judge between me and you.'

phrases.english: and it is written: "And Avraham came
to eulogize Sarah and to weep for her."
phrases.notes: This shows that שרה died before אברהם.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין: כָּל הַמּוֹסֵר דִּין עַל חֲבֵירוֹ הוּא נֶעֱנָשׁ תְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third item, מוסר דין על חבירו, from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That calling for judgment on another brings up one's own sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבין's teaching, based on שרה's words to אברהם (בראשית טז:ה) and her death before him (בראשית כג:ב).

steps.title: Four things that tear up a person's decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק lists four things that can tear up a bad decree against a person: צדקה, crying out in prayer, changing one's name, and changing one's deeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Four things tear up a person's decree. They are: צדקה, crying out, changing the name, and changing one's deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another list from רבי יצחק. This time it lists four things that can cancel a harsh judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After teaching what brings up sins, רבי יצחק now teaches what can save a person. Even after a decree has been sealed, these four things can tear it up. The next step will bring a פסוק for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: changing one's deeds for the better

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the source for the custom of giving a sick person an additional name, and it closely matches the famous phrase in the ימים נוראים תפילה: תשובה, תפילה וצדקה can remove a bad decree.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים מְקָרְעִין גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם,
phrases.english: Four things tear up a person's decree,
these are: charity, crying out,
changing the name, and changing one's deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים מְקָרְעִין גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement in the series. It is the opposite of step 7: what saves a person instead of what endangers him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקה, צעקה, שינוי השם and שינוי מעשה can tear up a person's decree.

steps.title: A פסוק for each of the four things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each item: צדקה saves from death, crying out brings rescue, שרה's name change brought her a son, and נינוה's changed deeds cancelled their destruction.
steps.simpleTranslation: צדקה, as it says: 'And צדקה saves from death.' Crying out, as it says: 'They cried to ה׳ in their trouble, and He took them out of their distress.' Changing the name, as it says: 'שרי your wife, do not call her name שרי, for שרה is her name,' and it says: 'I will bless her and also give you a son from her.' Changing deeds, as it says: 'And God saw their deeds,' and it says: 'And God relented from the evil He said He would do to them, and He did not do it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the list one by one and gives a source from תנ״ך for each item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two items each have one direct פסוק. For the name change and the change of deeds, the גמרא needs two פסוקים: one showing the change, and a second showing that the decree was then cancelled. שרה had been unable to have children until her name was changed, and the people of נינוה were saved after they did תשובה.

phrases.english: Charity, as it is written:
"And charity saves from death."
phrases.notes: משלי י:ב

phrases.english: Crying out, as it is written:
"And they cried to ה׳ in their trouble,
and from their distresses He brings them out."
phrases.notes: תהלים קז:כח

phrases.english: Changing the name, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״שָׂרַי אִשְׁתְּךָ לֹא תִקְרָא אֶת שְׁמָהּ שָׂרָי
phrases.english: "Sarai your wife, do not call her name Sarai,
for Sarah is her name,"
and it is written: "And I will bless her,
and I will also give you a son from her."
phrases.notes: After the name change, the decree that she could not have children was torn up.

phrases.english: Changing deeds, as it is written:
"And God saw their deeds,"
phrases.notes: יונה ג:י, about the people of נינוה.

phrases.english: and it is written: "And God relented from the evil

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶם וְלֹא עָשָׂה״.
phrases.english: that He said He would do to them, and He did not do it."

steps.triggerLanguage: צְדָקָה, דִּכְתִיב: וּצְדָקָה תַּצִּיל מִמָּוֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from תנ״ך for each of the four items listed in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Each of the four things that tear up a decree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משלי י:ב; תהלים קז:כח; בראשית יז:טו-טז; יונה ג:י.

steps.title: Some add a fifth: changing one's place
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion adds changing one's place of residence. The proof is that אברם was told to leave his land, and right after that he was promised he would become a great nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: also changing one's place, as it says: 'And ה׳ said to אברם: Go from your land,' and afterward: 'And I will make you into a great nation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion that adds a fifth item to רבי יצחק's list: moving to a new place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the order of the פסוקים. First אברם is told to leave his homeland, and right after comes the promise of becoming a great nation, even though until then he had no children. So moving away seems to have changed his fate.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion is the source of the well-known saying מְשַׁנֶּה מָקוֹם מְשַׁנֶּה מַזָּל, that changing one's place can change one's fortune.

phrases.english: And some say: also changing one's place,
as it is written: "And ה׳ said to Avram:
Go from your land,"
phrases.notes: בראשית יב:א

phrases.english: and afterward: "And I will make you into a great nation."
phrases.notes: בראשית יב:ב

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף שִׁינּוּי מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fifth item to רבי יצחק's list of four from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Changing one's place can also tear up a decree.

steps.title: Why רבי יצחק does not count changing one's place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יצחק would say אברם was helped by the merit of ארץ ישראל, not by the move itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי יצחק)? He would say: it was the merit of ארץ ישראל that helped him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יצחק would answer the proof from אברם, and explains why he did not include changing one's place in his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק agrees that אברם's fate changed. But he says the reason was not moving in general. It was the special holiness of ארץ ישראל, where אברם went. So this story cannot prove that any move changes a decree.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one (the opinion that disagrees)
helped him, was effective for him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק counts four things that tear up a decree: צדקה, צעקה, changing one's name, and changing one's deeds. The יש אומרים add changing one's place, but רבי יצחק says אברם was helped by ארץ ישראל, not simply by moving.

phrases.english: And the other one?
That was the merit of the Land of Israel
that helped him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ: הָהוּא זְכוּתָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא דְּאַהַנְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11, from רבי יצחק's point of view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from אברם that changing one's place tears up a decree.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אברם's change in fate came from the merit of ארץ ישראל, not from the move itself.

steps.title: A person must greet his רבי on a רגל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a person is obligated to go and greet his רבי on a רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: A person is obligated to greet his רבי on a רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יצחק, this time a practical obligation connected to the holidays. The next step brings his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shifts from teachings about judgment to a halachic duty. On a רגל a person should go visit his רבי. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: to go and greet one's teacher
one of the three pilgrimage festivals (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of visiting one's רבי on יום טוב, which is brought in הלכה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי רַבּוֹ בָּרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: A person is obligated to greet his teacher on a festival,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי רַבּוֹ בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching in the series of רבי יצחק's statements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is obligated to greet his רבי on a רגל.

steps.title: Proof from the שונמית's husband
steps.stepSummary: The husband of the שונמית asked why she was going to the נביא when it was not חודש or שבת. This implies that on those days she was expected to go.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Why are you going to him today? It is not חודש and not שבת.' This implies that on חודש and שבת she should have gone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי יצחק's rule from a פסוק in מלכים, and draws an inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband was only surprised because it was an ordinary day. That shows that on special days, going to visit the נביא was the normal, expected thing to do. From here we learn the duty to visit one's רבי on such days.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says חודש and שבת, but the rule is about a רגל. The גמרא understands שבת here as a holiday that is a day of rest, which is why it is used as a source for visiting one's רבי on יום טוב.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Why are you going to him today?
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ד:כג. The husband of the שונמית speaks about her going to אלישע.

phrases.english: It is not the New Moon and not Shabbat,"
which implies that on the New Moon and Shabbat
she was required to go.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: מַדּוּעַ אַתְּ הוֹלֶכֶת אֵלָיו הַיּוֹם לֹא חֹדֶשׁ וְלֹא שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural source for the rule stated in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The obligation to greet one's רבי on a רגל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב ד:כג, inferred from the husband's question to the שונמית.

steps.title: A person must purify himself for the Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that a person must make himself טהור on the רגל, based on the פסוק 'וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק also said: A person must purify himself on a Festival, because the verse says, 'And their carcasses you shall not touch.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a second teaching about the רגל. A person must make sure he is טהור (ritually pure) for the festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the רגל, Jews came to the בית המקדש and ate קרבנות, which requires טהרה. רבי יצחק reads the פסוק about not touching a נבילה as being about the festival. Right now he just states this. The next step will show why the פסוק must mean the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: to purify oneself, to become ritually pure
the carcass of an animal that was not slaughtered properly. Touching it makes a person ritually impure.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A person is obligated to purify himself
on a Festival,
as it is said: 'And their carcasses you shall not touch.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא יא:ח

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another teaching of רבי יצחק about the רגל. It follows his rule about greeting one's רבי on the festival.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must make himself טהור for the רגל.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows ordinary Jews are not normally barred from touching a carcass
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks whether the פסוק forbids all Jews from touching a נבילה. It answers no, since only the כהנים are warned about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. The verse says, 'And their carcasses you shall not touch.' You might think ordinary Jews are forbidden to touch a carcass. So the תורה says, 'Speak to the כהנים, the sons of אהרן.' This teaches that the sons of אהרן are warned, but ordinary Jews are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבי יצחק. The ברייתא first asks whether the פסוק forbids every Jew from touching a נבילה, and it says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the פסוק 'אֱמוֹר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן'. That פסוק warns only כהנים against becoming טמא. Ordinary Jews are therefore not warned. This sets up the question of what 'וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ' is for.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this. It introduces support from a source.
one might think. It introduces a possibility that will be rejected.

steps.confusionAlert: The 'יָכוֹל' line is not the ברייתא's conclusion. It is a possibility the ברייתא raises only in order to reject it.

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a ברייתא:
'And their carcass you shall not touch.'
One might think that Israelites are warned
against touching a carcass,
therefore the verse teaches:
'Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כא:א

phrases.english: The sons of Aaron are warned,
the children of Israel are not warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It brings a ברייתא to support רבי יצחק's reading of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's rule that the פסוק refers to the רגל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא contrasting 'וּבִנְבָלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ' with 'אֱמוֹר אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים'

steps.title: A קל וחומר shows the verse cannot be a year-round ban
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא argues with a קל וחומר. If ordinary Jews may touch a dead body, which is severe טומאה, they may surely touch a נבילה, which is light טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? Severe impurity, from a dead body, is forbidden to כהנים but not to ordinary Jews. So with light impurity, from a carcass, ordinary Jews should surely not be forbidden either.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves with simple logic that ordinary Jews cannot be forbidden to touch a נבילה. That makes the פסוק look unnecessary, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת מת, from a human corpse, is the most severe טומאה. Even so, only כהנים are warned against it. טומאת נבילה is milder, so ordinary Jews are surely allowed to touch a carcass. This leaves the question of what the פסוק forbidding contact is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stronger case (a fortiori)
severe impurity, here from a human corpse
light impurity, here from an animal carcass

phrases.english: But are these matters not a קל וחומר?
If with severe impurity,
priests are warned,
but Israelites are not warned,
then with light impurity, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא דְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It strengthens the point from the previous step and turns it into a question: why does the פסוק exist at all?
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ' as a general ban for all Jews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even corpse טומאה is allowed for ordinary Jews, the lighter נבילה טומאה must be allowed too. So a year-round ban makes no sense.

steps.title: The verse refers to the Festival
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that 'וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ' means that on the רגל, everyone must stay טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does the verse 'And their carcasses you shall not touch' teach? It teaches about the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the answer. The פסוק is about the רגל, which is exactly what רבי יצחק said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק cannot be an everyday ban, so it must apply to a special time. On the festival, all Jews go to the בית המקדש and need to be טהור. This confirms רבי יצחק's rule from step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: rather. It introduces the correct explanation.
what does the verse come to teach?

steps.whatToRemember: All Jews must make themselves טהור for the רגל. This is learned from 'וּבְנִבְלָתָם לֹא תִגָּעוּ', since that פסוק cannot be a year-round ban on ordinary Jews.

phrases.english: Rather, what does the verse teach when it says
'And their carcasses you shall not touch'?
It refers to the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the problem raised by the קל וחומר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק teaches that everyone must be טהור on the רגל, confirming רבי יצחק.

steps.title: Three books are opened on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי כרוספדאי, in the name of רבי יוחנן, teaches that three books are opened on ראש השנה: for the fully wicked, the fully righteous, and the in-between.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי כרוספדאי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Three books are opened on ראש השנה. One is for the completely wicked, one is for the completely righteous, and one is for people in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main theme, judgment on ראש השנה. It introduces a new teaching about three books.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People are sorted into three groups by their deeds. This step only names the groups. The next step explains what happens to each one.

keyTerms.meaning: people in the middle, whose good and bad deeds are balanced

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Kruspedai said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Three books are opened on Rosh Hashanah:
one of the completely wicked,
and one of the completely righteous,
and one of the in-between.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי כְּרוּסְפָּדַאי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It leaves רבי יצחק's festival teachings and returns to the topic of judgment on ראש השנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה, three books are opened for three types of people.

steps.title: The fate of each group
steps.stepSummary: The righteous are sealed for life right away and the wicked for death right away. The בינוניים stay undecided until יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The completely righteous are written and sealed for life right away. The completely wicked are written and sealed for death right away. The in-between wait, undecided, from ראש השנה until יום הכפורים. If they earn merit, they are written for life. If they do not, they are written for death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן's teaching continues and explains what happens to each of the three groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the בינוניים have a waiting period, the days from ראש השנה to יום הכפורים. Their actions during those days decide their fate. This is why the עשרת ימי תשובה are so important.
steps.whatToRemember: The fully righteous and the fully wicked are decided on ראש השנה. The בינוניים have until יום הכפורים to tip the scale.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea of the עשרת ימי תשובה as a window in which a person can change his judgment.

phrases.english: The completely righteous
are written and sealed immediately for life;
the completely wicked
are written and sealed immediately for death;
the in-between remain suspended
from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur;
if they merit, they are written for life;
if they do not merit, they are written for death.

steps.triggerLanguage: צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִין נִכְתָּבִין וְנֶחְתָּמִין לְאַלְתַּר לְחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the outcome for each of the three groups named in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The righteous and the wicked are sealed immediately. The בינוניים are judged by their deeds before יום הכפורים.

steps.title: רבי אבין finds the three books in a verse from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין shows that the פסוק 'יִמָּחוּ מִסֵּפֶר חַיִּים וְעִם צַדִּיקִים אַל יִכָּתֵבוּ' hints at three separate books.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said: Which פסוק teaches this? 'Let them be erased from the book of life, and let them not be written with the righteous.' 'Let them be erased from the book' is the book of the fully wicked. 'Of life' is the book of the righteous. 'And let them not be written with the righteous' is the book of the בינוניים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a פסוק behind רבי יוחנן's teaching about three books. רבי אבין splits one פסוק into three parts, and each part matches one book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece of the פסוק matches one group. 'Erased from the book' is the wicked, who are wiped out. 'Of life' is the righteous, who are written for life. 'Not written with the righteous' points to a third group that is written somewhere, just not with the צדיקים. That third place is the book of the בינוניים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asking for a source in תנ״ך)
Let them be erased / blotted out

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said: What is the verse?
phrases.notes: He is asking for the source of רבי יוחנן's teaching about three books.

phrases.english: "Let them be erased from the book of life,
phrases.notes: תהלים סט:כט

phrases.english: and let them not be written with the righteous."

phrases.aramaic: ״יִמָּחוּ מִסֵּפֶר״ — זֶה סִפְרָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִין,
phrases.english: "Let them be erased from the book": this is the book of the completely wicked,
"Of life": this is the book of the righteous,
"And let them not be written with the righteous":
this is the book of the in-between people.
phrases.notes: They are written in their own separate book, not together with the righteous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין, מַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for the three books described in steps 19-20.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching that three books are opened on ראש השנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים סט:כט, 'יִמָּחוּ מִסֵּפֶר חַיִּים וְעִם צַדִּיקִים אַל יִכָּתֵבוּ'

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק finds the three books in משה's prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different source: משה's words 'מְחֵנִי נָא מִסִּפְרְךָ אֲשֶׁר כָּתָבְתָּ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We learn it from here: 'And if not, please erase me from Your book that You have written.' 'Please erase me' is the book of the wicked. 'From Your book' is the book of the righteous. 'That You have written' is the book of the בינוניים.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers another פסוק as the source for the three books. He also splits it into three parts, one for each book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the source is משה's prayer after the חטא העגל. 'Erase me' matches the wicked, who are erased. 'Your book' is a special book that belongs to ה׳ Himself, so it is the book of the righteous. 'Which You have written' points to one more written book, the book of the בינוניים. The halacha does not change between the two sources; only the פסוק is different.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: From here:
phrases.notes: He offers a different פסוק as the source.

phrases.english: "And if not, please erase me
phrases.notes: שמות לב:לב, משה praying after the חטא העגל.

phrases.english: from Your book that You have written."
"Please erase me": this is the book of the wicked,
"From Your book": this is the book of the righteous,
phrases.notes: Called 'Your' book because it is ה׳'s special book.

phrases.english: "That You have written": this is the book of the in-between people.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק from רבי אבין's for the same teaching.
steps.raayaObject: The three books opened on ראש השנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות לב:לב, 'וְאִם אַיִן מְחֵנִי נָא מִסִּפְרְךָ אֲשֶׁר כָּתָבְתָּ'
steps.whatToRemember: Two אמוראים give two different פסוקים for the same idea: there are three books, one each for the righteous, the wicked, and the בינוניים.

steps.title: בית שמאי: three groups on the final Day of Judgment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes בית שמאי: on the great יום הדין there are three groups. The fully righteous are sealed right away for eternal life, and the fully wicked right away for גיהנם, based on a פסוק in דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: בית שמאי say there are three groups on the Day of Judgment: one of the fully righteous, one of the fully wicked, and one of the בינוניים. The fully righteous are written and sealed right away for eternal life. The fully wicked are written and sealed right away for גיהנם, as it says: 'Many of those who sleep in the dust will wake up, some to eternal life and some to shame and everlasting disgrace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the same three-group idea, this time for the great יום הדין at the end of days. The righteous and the wicked each get their final result right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דניאל lists only two results, eternal life and everlasting disgrace. These match the fully righteous and the fully wicked. The ברייתא says these two groups are decided immediately. The third group, the בינוניים, is handled differently, and the next step begins to explain how.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The Day of Judgment (here, the final judgment at the end of days)

steps.confusionAlert: This יום הדין is NOT ראש השנה. Steps 19-20 were about the yearly judgment on ראש השנה. בית שמאי are talking about the great judgment at the end of days, after the dead come back to life. That is why the פסוק speaks about people waking up from the dust.

phrases.english: It was taught: Beit Shammai say:
There are three groups for the Day of Judgment:
phrases.notes: The final judgment at the end of days.

phrases.english: one of completely righteous people,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִין, וְאַחַת שֶׁל בֵּינוֹנִיִּים.
phrases.english: one of completely wicked people, and one of in-between people.
Completely righteous people are written and sealed
right away for eternal life,
completely wicked people are written and sealed
right away for Gehinnom,
as it says: "And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will wake up,
phrases.notes: דניאל יב:ב

phrases.english: some to eternal life,
phrases.notes: The righteous.

phrases.english: and some to shame and everlasting disgrace."
phrases.notes: The wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the yearly judgment on ראש השנה to a similar three-group idea for the final יום הדין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the final יום הדין, the fully righteous are sealed right away for eternal life and the fully wicked right away for גיהנם.

steps.title: The in-between people go down to גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי begin to explain the third group: the בינוניים go down to גיהנם. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The בינוניים go down to גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now turns to the third group. This line is a setup, and the full explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בינוניים are not sealed right away like the other two groups. They go down to גיהנם, but only to be cleansed of their sins, not to stay there forever. The ending of the sentence, which tells what happens to them afterward, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: In-between people, whose good and bad deeds are about equal

phrases.english: In-between people go down to Gehinnom,
phrases.notes: To be cleansed. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּינוֹנִיִּים — יוֹרְדִין לְגֵיהִנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues בית שמאי's ברייתא by moving from the first two groups to the third group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בינוניים are not sealed right away. They go down to גיהנם to be cleansed.
